Bringing Manufacturing back to the US

📈 Secured Trillions of dollars in commitments to invest in the U.S.
📈 SoftBank promised $100 billion over four years, targeting AI and infrastructure, with a goal of 100,000 jobs, following a meeting with President Trump
📈 TSMC, one of the world’s leading chip makers, announced a $100 billion expansion of its U.S. operations, more than doubling its total U.S. investment.
📈 Roche plans to spend $50 billion on U.S. manufacturing and R&D
📈 Honda announced plans to shift production of its Civic from Japan to U.S. following tariffs
📈 Novartis plans to invest $23 billion in U.S. plants
📈 Nvidia announced plans to mass produce AI supercomputers in Texas as part of $500 billion U.S. push
📈 Johnson & Johnson is planning a $55 billion investment to expand U.S. manufacturing

And just on a secondary issue, in terms of artificial intelligence going into the space, have you all already seen that coming in, or is it something you are preparing for? And how is that going to affect the future of air traffic control- ling?

All of you have basically indicated what was stated either directly or indirectly that computational power and ability will dictate sort of the new criminal landscape. Obviously, AI will supercharge this. [...] I want to ask each of you, how far are we from having autonomous criminal behavior?
Jurisdictionally how do you see AI factoring into content actions, vehicles designed overseas that penetrate into the American market? How do we protect against that in a jurisprudence sense?

This is sort of a novel topic, but as each of you have stated clearly, this is a very important topic and development around the blockchain technology, AI technology, it is something that it is only going to become more prevalent and more dominant in just about every area of our life. That is true here in America; that is true overseas.

I'm very skeptical of people in big business who want to leverage big government to suppress competition. I'm afraid that's what we're seeing. That'd be like ... Google, Yahoo, Microsoft, Apple saying, 'We need to regulate all tech.' Whether it's software or hardware. It's like, guys, you're here already, right? And if there's one thing that I'm confident in, to protect AI for good, there has to be more than one option.
